# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

The terms in this book that a newcomer may not know, each with a short definition and the
section that explains it in context, where it comes with its reasons and an example. Code
and file names are listed by their letters, without punctuation.

::: glossary

::: glossary-letter
A
:::

adjusted Rand index (ARI)
:   A score of how far two groupings agree beyond chance: 1 means identical, 0 no better than chance. See @sec-choose-k.

`AGENTS.md`
:   A plain Markdown file of rules at the top of a project, which the assistant reads at the start of every session. See @sec-agents-md.

alt text
:   The description that screen readers announce, and that appears if an image cannot load. See @sec-md-link-image.

ALVA
:   The Association of Leading Visitor Attractions, the source of the London visitor counts; it counts only its member sites. See @sec-drift.

API
:   The vendor's programming interface; API prices are what a program pays per token when it calls a model directly. See @sec-choose.

::: glossary-letter
B
:::

blank line
:   A line with nothing on it. In Markdown it starts a new paragraph, and a list needs one above it. See @sec-md-basics.

block quote
:   A quotation set off from the text beside a bar, typed with `>` at the start of each line. See @sec-md-basics.

bootstrap
:   Refitting on rows drawn again at random, to test whether a result survives other data. See @sec-choose-k.

box plot
:   A box holding the middle half of a group's values, with lines at the median and the mean, and whiskers spanning the middle 90%. See @sec-compare.

branch
:   A movable label on a line of commits. See @sec-git.

::: glossary-letter
C
:::

catch-up box
:   The one line to paste into your assistant where the book reaches a checkpoint; after catching up, you carry on reading from the box. See @sec-catch-up and @fig-catch-up.

cell options
:   Instructions for a code cell in its first lines, written as comments that start with `#|`. See @sec-qmd-basics and @sec-cell-options.

checkpoint
:   A folder in the workshop's `checkpoints/` holding a project as it should be at the end of a hands-on block, with a README of catch-up steps. See @sec-catch-up and @fig-catch-up.

choropleth
:   A map whose areas are coloured by a value. See @sec-water-dashboard.

CI job
:   A build that a host such as GitLab runs on each push. See @sec-hosting.

cited copy
:   Facts typed into a source from a cited file; they do not follow the file when it changes. See @sec-md-table.

clone
:   To copy a repository, with its history, to your computer. See @sec-step-check.

cluster
:   A group of zone-years that are similar to each other on the chosen variables, found by k-means. See @sec-water-the-question.

code cell
:   A fenced block of code whose language is in braces, such as `{python}`; it runs when the document renders. See @sec-what-quarto and @sec-qmd-basics.

code fence
:   Three backticks that open and close a block of code; the word after them names the language, and the text inside is shown exactly as typed. See @sec-md-code-fence.

coding assistant
:   A program that writes files and runs commands at your request. See @fig-loop and @sec-model-harness.

command-line program
:   A program you run by typing a command in a terminal. See @sec-what-quarto.

commit
:   A recorded state of the project's files, with a message saying why it changed. See @sec-git.

CommonMark
:   A precise specification of Markdown, which GFM extends. See @sec-md-basics.

confounder
:   A third variable that affects both the exposure and the outcome, so the two move together even if one has no effect on the other. See @sec-confounders.

context
:   Everything sent to the model with a request: the conversation so far, the files read and the project's rules. See @sec-cost.

control
:   Comparing like with like, so a third variable cannot explain a difference; the clusters offer a partial control. See @sec-water-within.

correlation coefficient (r)
:   A measure from −1 to 1 of how two variables move together; 1 would mean they rise together along a straight line. See @sec-scaling.

CSV
:   A table in plain text, one line per row, with commas between the columns. See @sec-md-table.

::: glossary-letter
D
:::

dashboard
:   A page of charts and key numbers arranged in a grid. See @sec-content-once.

diff
:   The lines a change added and removed. See @sec-prompting.

difference-in-differences
:   Comparing places before and after a change with comparable places that did not change. See @sec-confounders.

display-only fence
:   A code fence whose language is not in braces, such as `python`: the code is shown and never run. See @sec-qmd-basics.

div
:   A block of Markdown between two lines of three colons, whose class in braces tells Quarto what to make of it. See @sec-content-once.

DIVIPOLA
:   DANE's list of Colombia's municipalities, which gives each a five-digit code: two digits for the department and three for the municipality. See @sec-water-data.

DOI
:   A document's permanent identifier; https://doi.org/ followed by it opens the publisher's page. See @sec-water-dashboard.

::: glossary-letter
E
:::

ecological fallacy
:   Drawing conclusions about people from data about places. See @sec-confounders.

effort
:   How long a model reasons before answering. See @sec-assistant.

elbow
:   The k after which inertia stops falling much. See @sec-choose-k.

environment
:   A folder holding one version of Python and the packages one project uses, kept apart from every other project's. See @sec-environments.

EPUB
:   An e-book format: a zipped set of web pages whose text reflows to fit the reader's screen. See @sec-formats-more and @sec-water-epub.

escape
:   A backslash before a Markdown mark, such as `\*`, which keeps the mark as typed. See @sec-md-basics.

Euclidean distance
:   Straight-line distance: the square root of the sum of squared differences across the features. See @sec-scaling.

`execute-dir`
:   A project setting that makes every page read files from the project folder. See @sec-water-website.

::: glossary-letter
F
:::

feature
:   A variable the clustering sees, and so one that defines the kinds. See @sec-water-features.

flag column
:   A column that marks every value that was filled. See @sec-prepare-steps.

freeze
:   Quarto's cache of computed results; with `freeze: auto` a page re-runs only when its own source changes, not when the data it reads change. See @sec-reproducible and @sec-water-website.

front matter
:   A block of settings in YAML between two lines of three dashes at the very top of a file. See @sec-qmd-basics and @sec-yaml.

::: glossary-letter
G
:::

`gh`
:   The GitHub command-line tool. See @sec-step-tools.

Git
:   The version-control tool: something like Track Changes for a whole folder, with a lasting history. See @sec-reproducible and @sec-git.

`git restore`
:   Puts a file back as it was at the last commit. See @sec-london-change.

GitHub
:   The website that keeps a copy of a repository online. See @sec-git.

GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM)
:   The dialect of Markdown GitHub uses for README files and issues: CommonMark with tables, task lists, strikethrough and automatic links. See @sec-md-basics.

`.gitignore`
:   The list of files and folders Git should not track. See @sec-london-website.

guard
:   A line that stops the render when a sentence's words, not only its numbers, no longer match the data. See @sec-water-website.

::: glossary-letter
H
:::

harness
:   The program on your computer that gives a model its tools, carries out its requests and asks you first. See @sec-model-harness.

home folder
:   Your own folder, written `~`. See @sec-step-terminal.

horizontal rule
:   A line across the page, typed as `---` between blank lines. See @sec-md-basics.

hyperparameter
:   A setting an algorithm cannot learn from its own objective, such as k. See @sec-choose-k.

::: glossary-letter
I
:::

impute
:   To fill a missing value with an estimate. See @sec-prepare-steps.

`index.qmd`
:   The source of a website's home page. See @sec-london-website.

inertia
:   The sum of squared distances from each point to its cluster's centre. See @sec-kmeans-steps.

infant mortality
:   Deaths under one year of age per 1,000 live births. See @sec-water-features.

inline code
:   Code in a sentence, such as `{python} name`, whose value Quarto writes into the sentence when the document renders. See @sec-what-quarto and @sec-qmd-basics.

IPM
:   The multidimensional poverty index: the share of a zone's people who are poor in several respects at once, from the 2018 census. See @sec-water-features.

IRCA
:   Colombia's risk index for drinking water, from 0, every test passed, to 100, every test failed. See @sec-water-why.

IRCA risk bands
:   Resolución 2115's five ranges of the IRCA: no risk, low, medium, high and unfit. See @sec-water-why.

::: glossary-letter
J
:::

join
:   Matching the rows of two tables by a column they share. See @sec-water-data.

Jupyter
:   The computation engine that runs Python code cells (knitr does the same for R). See @sec-what-quarto.

::: glossary-letter
K
:::

k
:   How many clusters k-means is asked to find. See @sec-kmeans-steps.

kernel
:   The running Python process that executes a document's cells, top to bottom. See @sec-render-mechanics.

k-means++
:   scikit-learn's way of choosing starting centres that are spread out, which makes a stuck start less likely. See @sec-kmeans-steps.

::: glossary-letter
L
:::

lead
:   The assistant session that starts sub-agents, waits for them and checks their results. See @sec-sub-agents.

line break
:   A new line inside a paragraph, made by ending the line with a backslash. See @sec-md-basics.

listing
:   A page that lists other pages, such as every post of a blog, made by Quarto. See @sec-water-website.

loadings
:   The weights of a principal component, which say what it measures. See @sec-water-pca.

lockfile
:   A file such as `uv.lock` that records the exact version of every package, for every system. See @sec-environments.

logarithm
:   A scale that measures ratios rather than differences: every doubling adds the same amount. See @sec-prepare-steps.

low-coverage
:   In a cluster's name, half a standard deviation or more below the year's average coverage: a relative position, not an absence of service. See @sec-names.

::: glossary-letter
M
:::

Markdown
:   A way of writing structured text with a few punctuation marks, such as `#` before a heading. See @sec-what-quarto and @sec-md-basics.

MDM
:   DNP's score of a municipality's management and results, from 0 to 100. See @sec-water-features.

median
:   The middle value, with half the values below it. See @sec-explore-what.

missing not at random
:   Gaps that depend on the unmeasured value itself, which no fill can repair. See @sec-water-bands.

model
:   A large language model: it reads and writes text and can reply with a request to use a tool. See @sec-model-harness.

monotonic
:   A relation in which one variable tends to rise as the other rises, though not necessarily along a straight line. See @sec-water-within.

municipality-year
:   One municipality in one year: the unit of the municipal outcomes, infant mortality and dropout. See @sec-outcomes.

::: glossary-letter
N
:::

naming rule
:   A written rule that names each cluster from its profile: setting, relative coverage and the band of its median IRCA. See @sec-names.

nano
:   The terminal's own simple text editor: Ctrl+O and Enter save, Ctrl+X leaves. See @sec-london-agents.

nominal pesos
:   Pesos not adjusted for inflation. See @sec-prepare-steps.

::: glossary-letter
O
:::

outcome
:   A variable the analysis only compares between the kinds and never clusters on. See @sec-water-features.

::: glossary-letter
P
:::

package
:   An add-on library that Python code imports, such as pandas for tables or matplotlib for charts. See @sec-environments.

Pandoc
:   The document converter inside Quarto that turns the executed Markdown into each output format. See @sec-what-quarto.

Pandoc's Markdown
:   The Markdown Quarto reads: GFM's core marks, plus attributes in braces, footnotes, definition lists, citations and mathematics. See @sec-md-basics.

Parquet
:   A file format for tables that keeps each column's type, so a code such as 05001 stays text. See @sec-compute-once.

PATH
:   The list of folders a terminal searches for programs, read when the terminal starts. See @sec-step-assistant.

percentile
:   The value below which a given share of the values lies; the 5th and 95th bound the middle 90%. See @sec-compare.

platform tag
:   The part of a package file's name that says which system and processor it was built for. See @sec-environments.

`pre-render`
:   A script Quarto runs before every render of a project, even of a single page. See @sec-water-website.

principal component
:   A direction in which the data vary: a weighted sum of the features. See @sec-water-pca.

principal component analysis (PCA)
:   A method that finds the directions in which the data vary most and projects the rows onto them. See @sec-water-pca.

profile
:   A cluster's mean of each feature over its rows, in z units. See @sec-heatmap.

prompt
:   The request you type into the assistant. See @sec-prompting.

Prompt, Check, Publish
:   The loop this book teaches: prompt an assistant for one small step, check what it did, and let Quarto rebuild every output from the checked source. See @fig-loop.

prompt (terminal)
:   The line ending in `$` (or `%` on a Mac) that shows the terminal is ready, and who and where you are. See @sec-step-terminal.

pull request
:   A proposal to merge a branch, which shows the difference line by line. See @sec-git.

push
:   Copying commits to the shared repository on GitHub. See @sec-git.

::: glossary-letter
Q
:::

`quarto preview`
:   Renders a file, serves it on a local address and renders it again every time the file is saved; Ctrl+C stops it. See @sec-md-basics and @sec-md-render.

Quarto project
:   A folder that a `_quarto.yml` file at its top turns into one website or book. See @sec-london-website.

::: glossary-letter
R
:::

random seed
:   The number that starts the computer's random-number generator, so random starts are the same on every run. See @sec-kmeans-steps.

raw block
:   A block that Quarto passes untouched to one format, such as a raw Typst block. See @sec-london-social.

render
:   To build a document's outputs from its source; `quarto render` executes, converts and typesets. See @sec-what-quarto and @sec-md-basics.

repository
:   A project folder with its Git history. See @sec-reproducible.

reproducible
:   Someone else, or you later, can rebuild the same results from the same files with one command, and see where every number came from. See @sec-reproducible.

root folder
:   The folder you start an assistant in, where it reads, edits and runs commands. See @sec-root-folder.

rural zone
:   A municipality's smaller settlements and dispersed countryside. See @sec-water-data.

::: glossary-letter
S
:::

Saber 11
:   ICFES's national exam for students finishing upper secondary school, with a global score from 0 to 500. See @sec-water-measures.

selection on the outcome
:   Keeping or dropping rows by the value being measured, so the rows kept are not typical. See @sec-outcomes.

self-supplied system
:   A water system that no utility runs. See @sec-water-why.

SGP
:   Colombia's system of national transfers to municipalities; the feature is its allocation for drinking water and sanitation, per person. See @sec-water-features.

ShareAlike
:   The condition of a CC BY-SA licence that anything built from the data is shared under the same licence. See @sec-water-ship.

shell
:   The program behind the terminal that runs your commands. See @sec-two-places.

silhouette
:   A score from −1 to 1 of how much closer each point is to its own cluster than to the next one, averaged over the points. See @sec-choose-k.

SIVIGILA
:   Colombia's public-health surveillance system. See @sec-water-stretch.

skewed
:   Mostly moderate values with a few very large ones. See @sec-prepare-steps.

slash command
:   A command such as `/model`, `/clear` or `/exit`, typed into the assistant itself. See @sec-cost.

small numbers
:   In small places a handful of deaths moves a rate a long way, so extreme rates are fragile. See @sec-outcomes.

Spearman's ρ
:   A measure, from −1 through 0 to +1, of whether two variables rise and fall together in rank order. See @sec-water-within.

standard deviation
:   Roughly, the typical distance of a value from the mean, in the variable's own unit. See @sec-prepare-steps.

static site
:   A folder of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images and documents, with no program running on a server. See @sec-hosting.

strikethrough
:   Text crossed out, written between two tildes on each side, `~~Car~~`. See @sec-md-basics.

sub-agent
:   A separate assistant session that your assistant starts for one task, with its own context. See @sec-sub-agents.

`sudo`
:   Runs a command as the administrator, after asking for your password. See @sec-step-ready.

SVG
:   A drawing written as text, which a model writes as it writes code. See @sec-assistant.

::: glossary-letter
T
:::

task list
:   A bulleted list whose items start with a box, `[ ]` empty or `[x]` ticked. See @sec-md-basics.

terminal
:   A window where you type commands instead of clicking. See @sec-step-terminal.

token
:   A fragment of text a few characters long: the unit models read, write and are priced by. See @sec-choose.

Typst
:   A modern typesetting system that ships inside Quarto and makes its PDFs. See @sec-what-quarto.

::: glossary-letter
U
:::

urban zone
:   A municipality's head town (cabecera municipal). See @sec-water-data.

utility-supplied IRCA
:   The IRCA of samples from systems a water utility runs ("prestadores"), which understates risk where people supply themselves. See @sec-water-why.

uv
:   The tool that installs Python and manages each project's packages. See @sec-step-tools and @sec-environments.

`uv run`
:   Runs one command in the project's environment, first bringing `.venv` up to date with `uv.lock`. See @sec-environments.

::: glossary-letter
V
:::

value box
:   A dashboard box that shows one key number with a label. See @sec-content-once.

variance
:   The square of the standard deviation. See @sec-scaling.

::: glossary-letter
W
:::

WebGL
:   The browser's built-in 3-D graphics. See @sec-london-3d.

WSL
:   The Windows Subsystem for Linux, which runs Ubuntu inside Windows. See @sec-setup.

::: glossary-letter
Y
:::

YAML
:   A format for settings in which indentation is meaning. See @sec-what-quarto and @sec-qmd-basics.

::: glossary-letter
Z
:::

zone variable
:   A variable measured separately for a municipality's urban and rural zones; a municipal variable has one value for the whole municipality, repeated on both rows. See @sec-water-features.

zone-year
:   One municipality's urban or rural zone in one year: one row of the water data, and Part III's unit of analysis. See @sec-water-data.

z-score
:   A value's distance from its year's mean, in standard deviations; it has no unit. See @sec-prepare-steps.

:::
